Sorting-free Projected Tetrahedra (SPT) was introduced as a technique to overcome the drawbacks of sorting-based projected tetrahedra methods, such as HAVS, which suffer from sorting errors and require extra buffer space [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that HAVS uses visibility sorting (k-buffer) and yields rendering artifacts due to sorting errors, and that SPT does not require visibility sorting, handles tetrahedral volumes without distinct artifacts, and requires no extra buffer space for candidate fragments. This directly supports the claim that SPT was introduced to overcome the drawbacks of sorting-based methods like HAVS, specifically sorting errors and extra buffer space requirements.
